abstract: This article looks at the advancements that have been made and the challenges that still lie ahead for fully utilizing the cloud in linear media operations. It examines the “lift and shift” perspective that still pervades most media technology and how cloud utilization is still being held back by operations wed to legacy workflows. We examine the most recent developments, especially those related to live production in the cloud. This article also examines two use cases that illustrate how fully leveraging cloud capabilities can transform linear media operations. The first looks at how to redesign playout in the cloud for scale while reducing cloud costs to a fraction of the costs of lift and shift. The second use case examines how volumetric cameras and an esports production model could transform live sports production in the cloud.

authors.bio: Peter Wharton is the chief strategy and cloud officer with TAG Video Systems, Tel Aviv, Israel, which makes innovative all-Internet Protocol (IP) monitoring systems. He is the founder of Happy Robotz LLC, Chesapeake Beach, MD, a media technology engineering, development, and consulting company that focuses on creating transformative cloud-based media operations through intelligent, cost-managed, and highly automated end-to-end workflows, and led the cloud migration project for a major U.S. network. He has also held a range of live production, product management, technology innovation, and business development roles with Grass Valley, Montreal, QC, Canada, Fox Television Networks, Washington, D.C., and American Broadcasting Company (ABC), Washington, D.C. He is a SMPTE Fellow and has previously served as SMPTE’s membership vice president, secretary/treasurer, and eastern regional governor and has produced the “Bits by the Bay” SMPTE Technology Conference, Washington, D.C., since 1999.
